hero_lede: Discover the story of my career's masterpiece in the AI age.
hero_role1: Roles — Product owner · UX designer · Front-end developer
hero_role3: Scope — UX strategy → design system → development → operation
hero_live_note: You are reading the live site right now.
hero_short: AI now drafts the résumés and the cover letters, so sounding capable has never been cheaper. A senior professional has to show the work instead, and I chose to lead that shift rather than wait for it. This site is my most advanced front-end build to date and the most important piece of my personal brand, designed and built by me with AI in five months. Scroll on for why it had to exist, how it grew from a single page, how it was built, and the figures that prove it.
act0_verdict: AI disrupts work. Careers can't adapt.
act0_lede: Three shifts that make a proven personal brand urgent in 2026.
act0_s1_t: A fifth of jobs in motion
act0_s1_x: By 2030, 22% of today's jobs will be disrupted: 170 million created, 92 million displaced, and 39% of core skills changing.
act0_s2_x: In Peru, 84% of tech employers demand AI modeling and app development. Pure designers now trail profiles who also build.
act0_s3_x: 66% of leaders would not hire someone without AI skills, and 71% would choose a less experienced candidate who has them.

act1_verdict: Credentials open doors. They don't prove design engineering skills.
act1_lede: Three reasons a strong résumé is no longer enough for differentiation.
act1_s1_x: Job posts spell out what a candidate must have, never how they think. Meeting every requirement gets an application read; being understood gets it believed.
act1_s2_x: A work sample predicts performance 3× better than education. This live page translates my credentials into proof of critical thinking and method.
act1_s3_x: Three in four hiring teams report AI-written applications, and 65% of hiring managers find skills harder to verify. Only a strong portfolio stands out with serious employers.
act1_foot: Sources: Sackett et al. (2022) on selection validity; Robert Half, November 2025, n = 2,000+; Deel Global Hiring Report 2026.
act2_verdict: Three levels of fidelity, one direction.
act2_lede: From renting a template to directing every code line.
act2_s1_x: My first portfolios ran on Canva, Figma and Framer. None matched the fidelity my UX authority demanded. Learning to code meant restarting as a junior programmer.
act2_s2_x: Not a prompt to brag about: weeks on one scroll gave me the flight hours no university could, locking the AI workflows behind this site.
act2_s3_x: The version accomplished after completing my Microsoft Front-End specialization. Home, About, and Contact pages, plus 4 copy-tested case briefs: my greatest build to date.
act2_foot: Building a site with AI in 2027 takes more than a prompt: it takes a whole orchestration, from research to review. That is what sets this build apart from audacious vibe-coders and from developers who still write every line by hand.

act4_verdict: Four choices keep this site scalable.
act4_lede: The technical stack across the page, in plain words.
act4_c1_t: 1) Light, fast and built to last
act4_c1_x: The site runs on the web's three core languages, with no framework so pages load fast and nothing breaks after a hard change.
act4_c1_rv_txt: Vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript: the web's native standards, with no framework, and no library, deployed as static files on GitHub Pages. No major-version migrations, no dependency to patch, full control of every byte, and a light payload that loads fast on an average phone.
act4_c2_x: Anyone can navigate with a keyboard or a screen reader, with text readable in light and dark themes, on a phone or a wide screen.
act4_c2_rv_txt: Built to WCAG AA: every meaningful image carries alt text, every control is reachable by keyboard with a visible focus state, and contrast is verified in both themes. Responsive layout resolves at three declared breakpoints: <767px, 768–1023px, and ≥1024px.
act4_c3_x: Every word lives in one of three dictionary types: text every page shares, text every case brief shares, and text for one page only.
act4_c3_rv_txt: Internationalization (i18n) runs on three layers of JSON dictionaries, merged in order: global for site chrome, regional for the strings every brief shares, local for each brief's own copy. Every string sits under one key at one level, and each English locale file has a Spanish twin with the same keys, checked by script. Spanish is transcreated, not translated.
act4_c4_t: 4) The same scaffold on every brief
act4_c4_x: Every case brief uses the same interface components as templates: editorials, cards, panels, charts and dashboards.
act4_c4_rv_txt: The web applies principles from Atomic Design and DesignOps. Global tokens for color, type and spacing feed atoms such as buttons and tags, molecules such as cards and reveal panels, and organisms such as this schedule and dashboard. Each brief builds the same organisms from its own data and dictionary, so one fix lands everywhere, and every change is checked at three page widths, two themes and two languages.

act6_lede: Learnings no academic title can provide.
act6_p1_x: A run stops at every gate until I release it. Review happens on the client server before changes are effective in live browser.
act6_p2_x: Every decision becomes a numbered ruling in one log, and every edit I make is recorded without a project controller.
